title: 4 BLACK & WHITE KITCHEN CANIST...
findings: Photo 2 backstamp (enlarged crop, print partly worn) reads TONGA / Stylecraft Fashion tableware by Midwinter / Staffordshire England, so the maker and pattern are not in the title. Four duos: matt black Fashion-shape cups with white interiors on squarish saucers printed with black and white zebra-type stripes. Sale listings I found date Tonga to the 1960s and credit Jessie Tait (unverified), so the title's 1950s is not confirmed. Four graduated cream moulded plastic canisters with sloped black lids, aluminium trim and gold script letters C, T, R and a fourth that reads as F or 7 (probably coffee, tea, rice, flour). No maker mark seen on the canisters, so they are not shown to be Midwinter.
condition: Cups and saucers look clean with no chips or cracks visible (one cup shown upside down). Canisters show light marks and wear. Lids, liners and the other saucer bases not inspected.
reason: Midwinter Stylecraft Tonga duos (maker not named in the title) with a matching-era plastic canister set, modest mid-century value.

title: LATE 1960'S CARVED BOOMERANG, ...
description: LATE 1960'S CARVED BOOMERANG, FEATURES KANGAROOS - BY IVY TANKS NALLARBOR WA - L-57 CM
findings: Photo 4 shows an old handwritten paper label stuck inside the curve, with tape patches: GENUINE ABORIGINE-MADE BOOMERANG FROM IVY TANKS - NULLARBOR W.A 17-1-1967. Ivy Tanks was a 1960s roadside cafe and petrol stop on the old Eyre Highway across the Nullarbor (Wikipedia, Old Eyre Highway page, which places it in South Australia although the label says W.A.). So the title's 'BY IVY TANKS' reads a place as the maker, and the 1967 date looks like a purchase date for a roadside souvenir, not a maker's date. Two kangaroos carved in relief on a chip-carved cross-hatched ground, plain bands with incised lines near one end, dark reddish hardwood with pale sapwood edges. No maker's name or signature. Length claim of 57 cm not checkable.
condition: Good for age: minor surface wear and small marks, no cracks or breaks seen. Label stained and held on with tape patches.
reason: Dated 1967 handwritten label ties it to the Ivy Tanks roadside stop; title mistakes the place for the maker; modest but documented Aboriginal-made souvenir boomerang.
marks_read: Handwritten label: GENUINE ABORIGINE-MADE BOOMERANG FROM IVY TANKS - NULLARBOR W.A 17-1-1967

title: A PAPUA NEW GUINEA SEPIK RIVER...

The reverse is hollowed with adze or gouge marks, a dark worn patina and a string loop, which supports hand carving. Sepik River origin is plausible by style but cannot be verified or dated from the photos; many such masks were made for the trade from the 1960s on, and the paint looks fairly fresh. Size claim (H-44 cm, W-24 cm) is consistent with the proportions.
condition: Paint mostly intact with wear to the white on the face and rim edges, small knocks to the edges. No major cracks or insect holes seen.
reason: Hand-carved painted cowrie-eyed Sepik-style mask; age and field use unproven, but decent examples have steady collector demand.

title: UNFRAMED WESTERN POLYNESIAN TA...
description: UNFRAMED WESTERN POLYNESIAN TAPA CLOTH BY MUA WALLIS H-53 L-200 CM
findings: Pictorial painted bark cloth (tapa) in two panels with wavy red-brown borders and a black and white geometric border. Upper panel: a house, three seated women with shell necklaces and flowers, a standing woman, pineapple, palms and flowers. Lower panel: sea creatures (lobster, crab, octopus, fish, ray) around an outrigger sailing canoe, with 'Mua Wallis' written on the sail (read in enlarged crops of photos 1 and 3). Mua is a district of Wallis (Uvea), so this looks like a place inscription, not an artist's signature, and the title's 'by Mua Wallis' misreads it. The composition closely matches Te Papa's pictorial Wallis and Futuna siapo FE012568 (https://collections.tepapa.govt.nz/object/1086286, seen 19/10/2026), which has the same sea-creature canoe scene with 'Mua Wallis' on the sail plus a house and women scene, is attributed to the 1960s and is described there as a rare pictorial type. This lot is narrower (about 53 cm against Te Papa's 76 cm) but the same type of piece. Age, and whether it is a later trade piece, are unverified. Black cloth hanging sleeves are stitched to both ends. Size claim (H-53, L-200 cm) is consistent with the proportions.
condition: Cloth looks intact with no holes or tears visible. Creases and folds, wavy uneven edges, a glossy varnish-like finish on the dark pigment areas. Small auction tag at one corner.
reason: Pictorial Wallis tapa matching a museum-documented rare type; title misreads the 'Mua Wallis' place inscription as a maker.
marks_read: Inscription 'Mua Wallis' on canoe sail (place, not signature)

title: 6 ROYAL DOULTON CABINET PLATES
findings: Six cabinet plates with photographic-style printed scenes (halftone screen visible): young kookaburras on a branch, a kangaroo with joey (sepia), a billabong with gum tree (two identical plates), a laughing bearded Aboriginal man with a red headband, and a gum tree with a snow-capped peak. The subjects match the Royal Doulton Australian Views series (dealers date it c.1953 to 1967, for example D6426 Young Kookaburras and D6422 Aboriginal), but no backstamps are photographed, so Royal Doulton and the series are not confirmed from the photos. One plate carries a handwritten tag reading 5200 (purpose unknown, ignored). No marks visible on the fronts.
condition: Prints and glaze look clean and unchipped in the photos. Backs and rims not shown, so crazing cannot be ruled out.
reason: Common Australian Views series plates with a duplicate, backstamps unseen, low value.
marks_read: Paper tag 5200 only, no backstamps shown
